failures.evidence: Real surface: throwaway rig (packages/daemon/internal/agentsecrets/zz_tester_daemon_test.go, removed; copy kept outside the tree) runs the daemon's agentsecrets.Client with its default schedules against the broker binary built at 7d770fb5, through a reverse-proxy front door, on the tester's Postgres 16, stopped with pg_ctl. 170 s outage: logins at 20:13:36 500, :38 500, :42 500, :51 500, 20:14:01 500, :11 429 RATE_LIMITED 'too many token logins for this ServiceAccount', :41 500, :43 429, 20:15:13 429, 20:16:13 500, :15 429; issued 17.8 s after Postgres was back. 40 s outage: 5x500 then 429, issued 23.8 s after Postgres was back. The gaps after a 429 are 30 s and 60 s, so a database that returns just after a 429 waits up to about a minute. Cause: limits.go:47 PerLogin {Every: 1 min, Burst: 5} is spent by refuseAccount after the token verifies and before the database write fails, so a 500 login costs a token. Red test committed in bcf37482: packages/envoy/internal/broker/api/token_login_test.go TestATokenLoginTheBrokerCouldNotCompleteSpendsNoAccountBucket (bucket of 2, store closed, four valid logins must all answer 5xx). `cd packages/envoy && BROKER_TEST_DATABASE_URL=... go test -count=1 -run TestATokenLoginTheBrokerCouldNotCompleteSpendsNoAccountBucket ./internal/broker/api` -> FAIL: 'the daemon's login 2 with the database away = 429 {"code":"RATE_LIMITED",...}'. A daemon-side change alone cannot meet ~10 s: the bucket refills one a minute.
